en: to be sticky; to be glutinous

examples.en: In summer, my body feels sticky because of sweat.
The floor is sticky, so someone must have spilled juice.
Your hands are sticky, so go wash them first.
Honey got on it, so the desk was sticky.
The sticky tape residue won't come off.
When the weather is humid, my skin feels sticky and uncomfortable.

explain: 손, 바닥, 피부에 무엇이 묻어서 달라붙는 듯한 불쾌한 느낌을 말할 때 많이 써요. '끈적끈적하다'와 비슷한데, 말할 때는 '몸이 끈적거려요'처럼 동사형도 자연스러워요. 깔끔하지 않은 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: My hands were sticky, so I went to wash them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끈적거리다'와 비슷한 상태를 나타내는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective describing a state similar to '끈적거리다'.

phrases.en: My back feels sticky from sweat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 느끼는 불쾌한 감촉을 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for an unpleasant feeling right now.

phrases.en: I wiped the sticky floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '끈적거리는'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '끈적거리는' to describe a noun that follows.

explain_en: It is often used for the unpleasant feeling of something clinging to your hands, floor, or skin. It is similar to '끈적끈적하다', and the verb form sounds natural in speech, as in '몸이 끈적거려요'. It usually carries a feeling of being unclean.

t90.ax: The sticky tape residue won't come off.

examples.en: The child lay flat on the floor.
The box got squashed flat when I stepped on it.
The cat pressed its ears flat.
I press the dough flat and bake it.
The balloon burst and shriveled up flat.
The bread sank flat, so it doesn't taste good.

explain: '납작'은 눌려서 넓고 얇아진 모양을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 형용사 '납작하다'와 함께 쓰이고, '납작 엎드리다'처럼 몸을 낮출 때 자주 나와요. '넓적하다'는 넓고 평평한 모양이고, '납작'은 눌려서 얇아진 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.example: 사장님이 화를 내자 직원들이 모두 납작 엎드렸어요.
phrases.en: keep one's head down; lie low
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 바닥에 낮춘다는 뜻에서 나와, 무서워서 눈치를 보며 조용히 숨죽이는 모습도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: From pressing the body flat, it also describes keeping a low profile out of fear or deference.

explain_en: 납작 imitates the look of something pressed wide and thin. It pairs with the adjective 납작하다 and often appears in 납작 엎드리다 (to lie flat). 넓적하다 means broad and flat, while 납작 adds a feel of being pressed thin.

t90.ax: The cat pressed its ears flat.

examples.en: In running, I'm second only to Minsu.

examples.ko: 한국에서 서울 다음가는 큰 도시는 부산이에요.
examples.en: The biggest city in Korea after Seoul is Busan.
When it comes to running, my younger brother is nearly as good as my older brother.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 실력으로 누구에게도 다음가지 않아요.
examples.en: That player is second to none in skill.

examples.ko: 이 팀에서 달리기는 지수 다음가면 제가 제일 빨라요.
examples.en: On this team, I'm the fastest runner after Jisu.

examples.ko: 작년 대회에서 제 기록은 민수 다음갔어요.
examples.en: At last year's competition, my record was second to Minsu's.

explain: '~에게 다음가다'나 '~ 다음가는 N'처럼 써요. '누구에게도 다음가지 않는다'는 제일이라는 칭찬이 되고, 같은 뜻으로 '둘째가라면 서럽다'라고도 말해요. 주로 순위나 실력을 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: Which city is second only to Seoul?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '두 번째로 큰/좋은 것'을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to mean 'the second-best' or 'second-largest'.

phrases.en: My cooking skills are second to none.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 제일이라는 칭찬이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it becomes praise meaning 'the best'.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 노래에서는 둘째가라면 서러운 사람이에요.
phrases.en: When it comes to singing, that friend is second to none.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다음가지 않다'와 같이 제일이라는 뜻으로 쓰는 자주 쓰는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common idiom meaning the same as '다음가지 않다': the very best.

explain_en: It is used as '~에게 다음가다' or '~ 다음가는 N'. '누구에게도 다음가지 않는다' becomes praise meaning the very best, and people also say '둘째가라면 서럽다' for the same idea. It mostly appears when talking about rank or skill.

en: to be uneven; to be ragged

examples.en: The weather has been unpredictable lately.

examples.ko: 들쑥날쑥한 출근 시간 때문에 생활이 불규칙해요.
examples.en: My irregular start times make my life irregular.
I'm upset because I cut my bangs unevenly.
My grades are inconsistent, so it's hard to set a goal.

examples.ko: 가게 문 여는 시간이 참 들쑥날쑥하네요.
examples.en: The shop's opening hours are really irregular.
Last month's sales were quite uneven.

explain: 일정하지 않고 이랬다저랬다 하는 상태를 말해서, 날씨, 시간, 성적, 컨디션에 두루 써요. 모양이 고르지 않을 때도 쓰고, 보통 '불규칙하다'보다 말투가 편해요. '들쭉날쭉하다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: I'm worried because of my uneven grades.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 일정하지 않은 대상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes a noun that is not consistent.

phrases.en: My sleeping times are irregular these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들쑥날쑥하다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '들쑥날쑥하다', so they are interchangeable.

phrases.en: My mealtimes are irregular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 격식 있고 글에도 쓰기 좋은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more formal and also suitable for writing.

explain_en: It describes a state that is not steady and keeps changing, so it fits weather, schedules, grades and condition. It also works for uneven shapes, and sounds more casual than '불규칙하다'. '들쭉날쭉하다' can be used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: Last month's sales were quite uneven.

examples.en: It's insanely hot today.
This tteokbokki is super spicy.
Yesterday's test was really, really hard.
I've missed you so much all this time.
I like that singer a whole lot.
The baby grows up incredibly fast.

explain: '아주', '정말'을 강하게 말하는 구어체 부사예요. 친구끼리나 편한 자리에서 쓰고, 글이나 발표에서는 '매우'가 더 어울려요. 더 짧게 '무지'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm really tired today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무지무지'를 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '무지무지' that is used even more often in speech.

phrases.en: This movie is really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 친구와 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and used casually with friends.

phrases.en: That person is really kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무지무지'보다 부드러워서 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '무지무지' and fine in most situations.

explain_en: It is a spoken adverb that intensifies '아주' or '정말'. Use it with friends or in casual settings; in writing or presentations '매우' fits better. It can also be shortened to '무지'.

examples.en: The book is worn out, so it doesn't look like much.
It doesn't look like much, but it tastes really good.
Please wrap the gift so that it looks nice.

examples.ko: 낡은 소파라도 천을 씌우면 볼품을 살릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even an old sofa can look decent if you put a cover on it.

examples.ko: 화분 하나만 놓아도 방 볼품이 달라져요.
examples.en: Just placing one plant changes how the room looks.

examples.ko: 작은 가게지만 간판이 예뻐서 볼품 있어요.
examples.en: It's a small shop, but the sign is pretty, so it looks good.

explain: 겉으로 보이는 모양새를 말하는데, 주로 '볼품이 없다'처럼 부정적으로 많이 나와요. '볼품 있다'도 쓰지만 '볼품없다'가 한 단어로 더 자주 쓰여요. 바로 이어서 쓰는 '볼품없다'와 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: The clothes are wrinkled, so they look shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼품'은 대부분 '없다'와 함께 써서 겉모양이 초라하다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '볼품' is mostly used with '없다' to say something looks shabby.

phrases.en: It's an old chair, so it looks shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼품이 없다'를 한 단어로 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '볼품이 없다' is also written as one word.

phrases.example: 볼품이 없지만 오래 쓸 수 있는 가방이에요.
phrases.en: It's not much to look at, but it's a bag you can use for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지만'으로 이어서 겉모양은 별로여도 장점이 있다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지만' you say the looks are poor but there is a good point.
phrases.en_equiv: although it isn't much to look at

explain_en: It refers to how something looks on the outside and often appears negatively, as in '볼품이 없다'. '볼품 있다' also exists, but '볼품없다' as a single word is used more often. Learn it together with '볼품없다'.

t90.ax: Please wrap the gift so that it looks nice.

examples.en: The autumn mountains are full of maple leaves in many colors.
The children run around holding balloons of every color.

examples.ko: 꽃집 앞에 색색으로 물든 꽃들이 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Flowers in all kinds of colors are set out in front of the flower shop.

examples.ko: 색색 고운 한복을 입고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took photos in a hanbok of lovely colors.
Fireworks of many colors burst in the sky.
Beads of many colors scattered across the floor.

explain: 여러 가지 색깔이 섞여 있는 느낌으로, 주로 '색색의 + 명사'로 써요. 글이나 묘사에서 잘 어울리고, 말할 때는 '여러 색'이나 '알록달록'이 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: Flowers of many colors have bloomed in the garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: '색색의' 뒤에 명사를 붙이는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, with a noun after '색색의'.

phrases.en: There are many colorful clothes in the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '색색'보다 '알록달록'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, '알록달록' sounds more natural than '색색'.

phrases.en: I decorated my notebook with pens of many colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest option to use in daily conversation.

explain_en: Each item in its own color, like flowers in a garden (색색의 꽃); everyday. It gives the feel of many different colors mixed together and is mostly used as '색색의 + noun'. It suits writing and description, while in speech '여러 색' or '알록달록' often sounds more natural.

examples.en: The students are waiting in a single line.
Please put the chairs in a row.
The duck family crosses the road in a line.
The path is narrow, so we have to walk in single file.

examples.ko: 책을 일렬로 꽂았더니 정리가 잘 됐어요.
examples.en: After lining the books up in a row, it looked neat.

examples.ko: 탁자 위에 컵이 일렬로 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: The cups are lined up on the table.

explain: 일렬은 한 줄을 말하고 '일렬로'로 거의 부사처럼 써요. 가로 줄은 '행', 세로 줄은 '열'이라고 하는 말과 달리 일렬은 방향 구분이 없어요. 줄을 서는 일은 '줄을 서다'라고 많이 해요.

phrases.en: The children stood in a line in front of the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 한 줄을 이루어 설 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for people standing in a single line.

phrases.en: My friends are sitting in a row.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앉아 있는 모습이 한 줄로 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people sit lined up in one row.

phrases.en: Please line up in a single line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일렬로와 같은 뜻인데, 말할 때는 '한 줄로'가 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 일렬로, but 한 줄로 is easier and more natural in speech.

explain_en: One straight row, one behind another — queues, lined-up students. 일렬 means one line and is almost always used as the adverbial '일렬로'. Unlike '행' (row) and '열' (column), 일렬 doesn't specify direction. For queuing up, people usually say '줄을 서다'.

dis.h: one single straight row, one behind another

p.n: 대열 is not used with 로 to mean 'in a row'; it means a formation of ranks.

examples.en: It's the best restaurant in our neighborhood.
He is the top expert in this field.
They say it used to be the wealthiest family of all the rich ones.

examples.ko: 그 집 김치 맛은 이 시장에서 제일간다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: That shop's kimchi is rumored to be the best in this market.

examples.ko: 제일갈 만한 실력이 아니면 뽑히기 어려워요.
examples.en: Unless your skill is among the very best, it's hard to get chosen.
Even the richest person was poor as a child, they say.

explain: '제일가는 + 명사' 모양으로 가장 많이 써요. '제일 좋다'보다 한 범위 안에서 으뜸이라는 느낌이 강해서 '이 동네에서 제일가는 맛집'처럼 범위를 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: He is the richest person in this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제일가는' 뒤에 사람이나 직업을 붙여서 으뜸인 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a person or job after it to name the top one.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 나라에서 제일가는 실력을 갖고 있어요.
phrases.en: That player has the best skill in the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이나 솜씨가 가장 뛰어날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's ability or skill is the best.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 한때 동네에서 제일가던 빵집이었어요.
phrases.en: This shop was once the best bakery in the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 으뜸이었던 것을 말할 때는 '제일가던'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '제일가던' for something that used to be the best.
phrases.en_equiv: that used to be the best

explain_en: It is most often used in the form '제일가는 + noun'. Rather than a plain '제일 좋다', it carries the feeling of being at the top within some range, so the range is usually stated, as in '이 동네에서 제일가는 맛집'.

en: to be gentle and well-mannered; to be neat

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 참하고 성실해 보여요.
examples.en: The new employee looks neat and diligent.
I'd like to introduce you to a nice, well-mannered person.
That young woman is gentle both in looks and in heart.

examples.ko: 참하게 앉아 있는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see him sitting there so properly.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 참하다는 칭찬을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: My daughter is often praised for being well-behaved.
The child who used to be so well-behaved has become mischievous lately.

explain: 모습이나 성격이 얌전하고 단정하고 착실할 때 써요. '착하다'와 달리 단정하고 얌전한 겉모습까지 포함해요. 어른들이 젊은 사람을 칭찬할 때 자주 들을 수 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I'm glad to have met a decent, gentle person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얌전하고 단정한 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone gentle and neat.

phrases.en: That student is well-behaved and diligent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참하다'를 다른 좋은 성격과 함께 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links 참하다 with other good traits.

phrases.en: The new neighbor seems nice and proper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 받은 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses an impression based on appearance.

explain_en: It is used when someone's appearance or character is gentle, neat and steady. Unlike '착하다', it also includes a tidy, modest look. You often hear it when older people praise a young person.

en: to be unique; to be peculiar; to be characteristic

examples.en: This food has its own distinctive smell.
That person talks in a way all their own.

examples.ko: 한국 문화에 특유하다고 할 만한 표현이에요.
examples.en: It's an expression you could call unique to Korean culture.
I like this cafe's distinctive atmosphere.

examples.ko: 이 식물은 이 지역에서만 자라서 이곳에 특유해요.
examples.en: This plant grows only in this region, so it is unique to this place.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 다른 곳에 없는 특유한 풍습이 있어요.
examples.en: This island has a distinctive custom found nowhere else.

explain: '특유의 맛', '특유의 냄새'처럼 '특유의'를 명사 앞에 쓰는 형태가 더 자연스러워요. '~에 특유하다'는 어떤 곳이나 사람에게만 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 비슷한 '독특하다'는 다른 것과 다르다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: This kimchi has its own distinctive taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특유하다'는 이렇게 '특유의'로 명사 앞에 쓸 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 특유하다 sounds natural in the form 특유의 before a noun.

phrases.en: This shop has a peculiar smell of its own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것에서만 나는 고유한 냄새를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A smell that belongs to that particular thing.

phrases.en: This cafe has a unique atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특유하다'와 비슷하지만 다른 것과 다르다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but with a stronger feel of being different from others.

explain_en: Typical trait of a specific item or person, like a signature smell. '특유의 맛' and '특유의 냄새' (its distinctive taste and smell), with '특유의' before a noun, is the most natural form. The pattern '~에 특유하다' means something found only in one place or person. The similar '독특하다' puts more weight on being different from others.

t90.ax: This food has its own distinctive smell.

en: to scatter; to dishevel; to rumple

examples.en: The child scattered toys all over the room.
The wind messes up my hair.

examples.ko: 큰 소리가 집중을 흐트러뜨리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that loud noises don't break your concentration.

examples.ko: 정리한 책을 또 흐트러뜨리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not mess up the books I arranged again.
He left, strewing clothes here and there.
There were many things that could unsettle my mind.

explain: 정돈된 것을 일부러든 실수로든 어지럽게 만들 때 써요. 저절로 어지러워지면 '흐트러지다'라고 하고, 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. '흐트러트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling scattered the papers on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흐트러뜨리다'와 같은 뜻인 다른 표기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An alternate spelling with the same meaning as '흐트러뜨리다'.

phrases.en: Don't slouch during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바른 모습을 흐트러지게 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means letting a proper posture fall apart.

phrases.example: 큰 소리가 공부할 때 집중을 흐트러뜨려요.
phrases.en: Loud noises break my concentration when I study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 집중처럼 추상적인 것에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for abstract things like concentration, not just objects.

explain_en: Someone makes things messy on purpose or by accident. It is used when you make something that was neat messy, on purpose or by accident. When it becomes messy by itself, use '흐트러지다', so learn them as a pair. '흐트러트리다' is also used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: The wind messes up my hair.

examples.en: The farmer feeds hay to the cows.
The warehouse is full of piled-up hay.
The horse smelled the hay and came closer.
Hay gets moldy if it gets wet in the rain.
This cushion is stuffed with hay.
The children played on top of a pile of hay.

explain: 소나 말 같은 가축의 사료로 쓰려고 베어서 말려 둔 풀이에요. 벼 같은 곡식을 거둔 뒤에 남는 줄기인 '짚'과는 달라요. 일상에서는 '말린 풀'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 마당 한쪽에 건초 더미가 쌓여 있어요.
phrases.en: A pile of hay is stacked in one corner of the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더미'가 붙으면 건초가 높이 쌓인 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '더미' describes hay piled up in a heap.

phrases.en: In summer, they cut grass and make hay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀을 베어 말려서 사료로 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means cutting and drying grass to prepare feed.

phrases.en: The horses happily eat dried grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건초'를 쉽게 풀어 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to explain what '건초' is.

explain_en: It is grass that has been cut and dried to feed livestock such as cows and horses. It differs from '짚' (straw), the stalks left after harvesting grain like rice. In daily talk people sometimes just say '말린 풀' (dried grass).

examples.en: A hedgehog has spines on its body.
My friend keeps a hedgehog as a pet.
The hedgehog got scared and curled into a ball.
I almost got pricked by a hedgehog's spines.

examples.ko: 고슴도치와 토끼 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like more, a hedgehog or a rabbit?
I saw a picture of a cute hedgehog.

explain: 고슴도치는 가시 때문에 속담에도 나오는 동물이에요. 비슷하게 가시가 있는 '호저'는 몸이 더 크고 가시도 길어서 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 아무리 말썽쟁이여도 부모에게는 예뻐요. 고슴도치도 제 새끼는 함함하다고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Even a hedgehog thinks its own young are silky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자식은 누구에게나 예뻐 보인다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning every parent thinks their own child is lovely.
phrases.en_equiv: every crow thinks its own young the fairest

explain_en: The hedgehog appears in a Korean proverb because of its spines. A 호저 (porcupine) also has spines but is bigger with longer quills, so it is a different animal.
